facts.text: On this date in 1990, East and West Germany reunified — absorbing a country of 16 million people, yet Berlin still bears more construction cranes today than any other European capital.
On this date in 1932, Iraq became the first Arab country to gain independence, though Britain quietly retained control of its military bases and oil concessions for decades after.
More people live inside a 40-mile radius of Manila than in the entire country of Australia.
The Sahara Desert was green savanna with lakes and hippos as recently as 5,000 years ago — well within the span of human civilization.
Canada has more lakes than every other country on Earth combined, containing roughly 60% of the world's fresh surface water.
On this day in 1995, Barings Bank's Nick Leeson was arrested in Frankfurt — the rogue trader who single-handedly bankrupted Britain's oldest merchant bank with $1.3 billion in hidden losses.
On October 3, 1929, the Dow peaked at 381 — a level it would not revisit for 25 years. The crash that followed wiped out roughly 90% of market value by 1932.
The S&P 500 has returned roughly 10% annually for a century, yet the average investor captures less than half that — mostly by buying high and selling low.
Saudi Aramco paid out more in dividends in 2023 than Apple, Microsoft, and Google combined. One company. One country. One commodity.
The Dutch East India Company, the first corporation to issue public stock, was at its peak worth an estimated $8 trillion in today's dollars — dwarfing every company alive.
On this date in 1962, Wally Schirra orbited Earth six times in nine hours. His pulse never exceeded 90 bpm — calmer than most people stuck in traffic.
On this date in 1990, East and West Germany reunified. The gravitational pull of the newly combined landmass did not change by a single measurable unit.
Your skeleton is not the rigid cage it appears. Bone is a living tissue that completely replaces itself every decade, meaning the skeleton inside you now did not exist ten years ago.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
The mantis shrimp sees sixteen types of color receptors compared to the human eye's three — yet research shows it is worse at distinguishing similar shades, suggesting more is not always more.
On this day in 1990, East and West Germany reunified — an event older than the entire World Wide Web being publicly available to civilians.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded.
On this day in 1863, Lincoln declared Thanksgiving a national holiday. The turkey-and-gratitude ritual is younger than the machine gun.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid.
The fax machine was patented in 1843 — before anyone had photographed a living US president, and 23 years before the first transatlantic telegraph cable worked reliably.
Meraki (μεράκι): Greek for doing something with soul, creativity, or love — leaving a piece of yourself in your work. No clean English equivalent exists.
Sonder: the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined in 2012; already feels ancient.
Hiraeth (Welsh): a homesickness for a home you cannot return to — or that never was. The longing and the grief arrive together.
On this date in 1990, German reunification took effect, and with it, Ostalgie entered the lexicon: nostalgia for life in the former East Germany, born the moment it disappeared.
Ubuntu (Zulu/Xhosa): 'I am because we are.' A single word carrying an entire philosophy of shared humanity that Western languages require a paragraph to approximate.

On this date in 2013, Silk Road was seized by the FBI. The 144,000 BTC confiscated — worth ~$28M then — would peak above $9B a decade later, making it one of the most valuable law enforcement forfeitures in history.

On Oct 3, 2011, Litecoin's genesis block was mined. Charlie Lee designed it to produce blocks 4x faster than Bitcoin and used Scrypt specifically to resist the ASIC hardware that was centralizing Bitcoin mining.

Bitcoin's UTXO model means your wallet balance doesn't exist on-chain. What exists are discrete unspent outputs — each a lockbox. 'Sending bitcoin' really means destroying old lockboxes and creating new ones.

The Ethereum merge in 2022 cut the network's energy use by ~99.95%. It did not speed up transactions, lower fees, or change the block size — nearly every popular claim about its effects at launch was wrong.

Satoshi's known addresses hold roughly 1.1 million BTC, unmoved since mining. Because they span early 2009 blocks mined with a specific extraNonce pattern, researchers can fingerprint them as almost certainly one entity.

On this date in 1997, Garry Kasparov formally filed a protest over Deep Blue's move 36 in Game 2 — a quiet bishop retreat IBM engineers later admitted was caused by a bug, not strategy. Kasparov never played it again.

On this date in 2003, the DARPA Grand Challenge course was quietly finalized — a 142-mile Mojave route no robot would finish the following March, with the best entry covering just 7.4 miles before beaching on a berm.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 GWh of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of 4,500 average US homes, all spent before a single user query was served.
AlphaFold 2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins in its 2022 database release. The entire prior history of experimental crystallography had resolved roughly 190,000.
Transformers were introduced in 2017 by a team of eight researchers, six of whom have since left Google. The architecture now underlies nearly every major language and vision model in production.
